capabilities.§267: The workflow now FUNCTIONS against a real product observation. §266 measured every Expert run from the shipped client failing 409 after a provider leg, because the panel only renders once a deterministic analysis exists and the client hardcoded requestVersion 1. §267 removed client-side sequencing entirely and proved the repair with a request body constructed by expertApi.ts itself, posted onto an observation already carrying a deterministic analysis.

capabilities.capability: Downstream authority guard on finding finalization
capabilities.evidence: verification/expert-hazlenz-265-frontend-product-workflow-2026-09-12/SECTION-265-ACCEPTANCE.json cases L, M, N
capabilities.productConsequence: a finding cannot be finalized from an Expert analysis whose operational conclusion no person has settled; once settled, the SAME review finalizes, and an override is consumed as the human value rather than the Expert proposal
capabilities.boundary: ONE consumer. The deterministic path is untouched — a review citing no analysis, or a client_supplied one, is unaffected. Completion readiness, report finalization, notifications and the executive summary are not yet guarded.
capabilities.§267: SCOPED TO FINALIZATION. The gate no longer runs on the dismissal branch: dismissal rejects the proposed finding and consumes no operational conclusion, so requiring Expert settlement first was over-restriction. Finalization remains gated, unchanged.

capabilities.§267: It is now the ONLY route that serves Expert analysis content. GET /inspections/:id previously returned server_authored resultSnapshot rows whole behind JwtGuard alone; it now projects them to lifecycle metadata with the snapshot withheld.

capabilities.capability: Pre-spend adjudication of Expert execution identity
capabilities.evidence: verification/expert-hazlenz-267-product-integration-defect-closure-2026-09-13/ — cases PRE-1..6, measured as a provider-entry DELTA of 0 across the refused requests
capabilities.productConsequence: A stale or invented execution version is refused before the transport is reachable, so a conflicting request costs nothing. This extends the §261 pre-spend claim from "duplicate identity" to "conflicting version".
capabilities.boundary: It bounds waste on KNOWABLE conflicts only. It is not a spend ceiling: NO_SPEND_CEILING_OR_KILL_SWITCH remains an open P0 and total Expert cost is still unbounded.
capabilities.nextAction: the per-workspace spend ceiling and the explicit Expert enable flag

betaReadinessDomains.note: A BLOCKER domain does not mean the domain is architecturally wrong. Every one of the ten maps to a finite item in BETA-BLOCKERS.json, and none requires redesign.
betaReadinessDomains.§267: Domain 4 moves BLOCKER -> READY: the two P0 defects that made the shipped Expert workflow non-functional are closed and proven against the real client request path. Domain 5 (downstream authority containment) keeps READY_WITH_ACCEPTED_LIMITATION, but the limitation is now smaller — the inspection-payload bypass that made containment a property of what happens to be written rather than of a guard is closed. Every other domain is unchanged; §267 touched no infrastructure, operations or legal surface.
